- Proof of cancellation at least one day before the trip or event and any charges
- Original receipts and invoices

- Contagious disease: a medical certificate showing quarantine is required, or a copy of the test results
- Death: a copy of the death certificate
- Quarantine: a copy of the official document that places you or your travel companion in quarantine due to an epidemic or pandemic
- Childbirth: a copy of the birth certificate
- Redundancy: a copy of your company's redundancy notice, proof of your employment contract, and the exact start date of your employment
- Traffic accident: a copy of the breakdown, towing invoice, or report, and a medical report if any medical attention was needed
- Theft of identity papers or tickets: a copy of the police report and any other documents showing your efforts to replace the stolen items

- Open your device's settings and select 'Connections'
- Tap 'Mobile networks' and choose 'Access Point Names'

- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu
- Tap 'eSIM' and 'Get data plan'
- Choose your desired coverage — local for one country, or regional/global for multiple countries
- Select the amount of data you need
- Proceed to check out and purchase your plan

## How to check how much data you've used
In the Revolut app:
- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu
- Tap 'eSIM' and select one of your active plans
- You'll see the remaining data and total data used

To remove the Revolut eSIM on iOS, go to your device settings, select ‘Mobile service’, then ‘SIMs’, choose the Revolut eSIM, and select 'Delete eSIM'.

- Navigate to SIM or network settings
- Select the eSIM you want to remove
- Look for an option to remove or delete the SIM

- Select eSIM and choose 'Get data plan'
- Select a coverage — local for one country, or regional or global for multiple countries
- Select data amount
- Continue to checkout

The data plan’s validity period starts from the date of purchase, or when your eSIM is ready to be installed if it’s your first purchase. To request a refund, you need to contact us via our in-app chat. You can have up to 15 eSIM data plans, but only one can be used at a time.

- Select 'Global'

- Insufficient funds
- Security concerns, like if your card has been reported lost
- Transactions aren't supported by the issuing bank

- Tap '+' in the top-right corner
- Select 'Debit or Credit Card'

In-app verification:

- Tap 'Confirm'
Text message verification:
- Tap the notification sent to your phone where the Revolut app is installed
- You’ll be automatically redirected to log in to the Revolut app

Rest of the world: Australia, Brazil, Japan, Mexico, New Zealand, Singapore, US.

- iPhone SE or more recent models
- iPad 3 or newer models
- All Apple Watch models
- Mac models with Touch ID

- Have passed identity verification
- Have no negative balance on the account
- Use a non-disposable (physical or virtual) card
- Be the minimum age required to use Apple Pay in your country

A Direct Debit is when you authorise someone else to withdraw from your account at regular intervals. Usually, Direct Debits are set up to pay rent, bills, or mortgages. Direct Debits are only available for local EUR and GBP transfers.

## Insufficient funds for a Direct Debit
If you don’t have enough funds in the Direct Debit currency, we’ll check other currency balances in the order below, and take the full amount from the first one with enough funds. We can’t combine multiple currencies to complete the payment. We'll check your accounts for funds in this order:
- Transaction currency
- Your base currency
- Next active currency with enough balance
If no currency has enough funds in the order above, the Direct Debit will fail. You can customise your preferred currency for a specific Direct Debit in the 'Scheduled payments' section of the Revolut app.

## Direct Debit didn't trigger
There are a few reasons why a Direct Debit might not have been processed when you were expecting. It could have been previously deactivated, or the merchant may have scheduled it for a different date. To check if the Direct Debit is still active, and to verify its scheduled date:
- Go to 'Payments' on the bottom menu
- Tap the calendar icon in the top-right corner
- Choose the transaction to view the scheduled charge date
If you can't see the transfer, it was either disabled, or it wasn't successfully created in the first place. In these cases, contact the merchant directly to clarify the situation, or set it up again.

## Direct Debit failed or reverted
Check to see why your Direct Debit failed or was reverted in your transactions list. Just tap on the unsuccessful transaction for more info.

## Dispute a Direct Debit
Tap ‌the Direct Debit in your transactions list and choose the problem you're experiencing. You can then follow the prompts to dispute the Direct Debit.

## View and manage my subscriptions
- Go to 'Payments' on the bottom menu 
- Tap the calendar icon in the top right corner
- Select a subscription to view its details

- Go to your transaction historyhttps://app.revolut.com/transactionsrevolut://app/transaction-list
- Tap on the payment to open its details
- Toggle 'Subscription payment'

## How to prevent a subscription from happening again
- Block a specific subscription payment to a merchant: only subscription payments of the specified amount of that merchant will be blocked
- Block the merchant: all payments to this merchant will be blocked

## How to block a subscription in-app
- Tap your profile icon in the top-left corner 
- Select 'Security'
- Choose 'Payments' and 'Blocked payments'
- Tap 'Add new' above 'Subscriptions' or 'Merchants' sections and select a previous payment from the merchant you want to block
To unblock the merchant, select the merchant you want to unblock and tap 'Unblock payments'. If you still don't see the subscription as unblocked, follow these steps:
- Go to your transaction list https://app.revolut.com/transactionsrevolut://app/transaction-list
- Tap the payment to the merchant you want to unblock
- Tap 'Unblock payments'

## How to cancel a subscription
To cancel a subscription, you'll need to contact the merchant. Blocking a subscription or a merchant  in-app doesn't cancel the subscription.
Blocking future payments to a merchant on our platform prevents them from collecting subscription payments based on their merchant ID and specific amount.

In your Revolut app:
- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu of the Revolut app
- Go to the 'eSIM' section
- Follow the steps below

- Open settings and choose 'Networks & Internet'
- Select 'SIMs (+)' and then select a SIM
- Tap 'Next' on the 'Download your eSIM' page
- Tap 'Need help?' on the 'Scan your QR code from network page'
- Tap 'Enter it manually' on the 'Help adding a network page'
- Enter ‌the code you receive and select 'Continue', before tapping 'Download'

- Select the Revolut eSIM for data roaming from your device’s settings

- Open 'Settings' and select 'Mobile Service'
- Under 'SIMs', select your newly installed eSIM (your device may automatically name your eSIM, but it won’t be your 'Primary' SIM)

- Proceed to check out and purchase your plan

- Navigate to SIM or network settings
- Select the eSIM you want to remove
- Look for an option to remove or delete the SIM

eSIM data plans can only be used on the device they were purchased from. You can't use them on another device, even if you've downloaded the Revolut app on that device.

- Select 'Global'

1. Vai alla schermata 'Home' nel menu in basso.

3. Inserisci l'importo.
4. Sotto l'importo, scegli il metodo di pagamento.
5. Imposta la valuta sulla valuta locale della tua carta per evitare commissioni di cambio.
6. Seleziona una carta salvata. Se vuoi aggiungere un'altra carta, tocca 'Carta di debito'.

## Reasons for the temporary block
Some common reasons which lead to these payment blocks are:
- Insufficient funds
- Security concerns, like if your card has been reported lost
- Transactions aren't supported by the issuing bank

- The transfer needs to be reviewed to meet regulatory requirements

- The transfer details were incorrect or incomplete (e.g. a missing reference number)
- We requested missing personal information for your Revolut account and didn't receive it in time

The funds will automatically be returned to the sender, but the timeframe depends on the transfer type. Revolut cannot speed up this process as it depends on the sending bank and any intermediary banks.
- Domestic transfers: should arrive back in the sender's account within 5 business days
- International (SWIFT) transfers: can take up to 15 to 20 business days due to the multiple intermediary banks involved

## Insufficient funds for a Direct Debit
If you don’t have enough funds in the Direct Debit currency, we’ll check other currency balances in the order below, and take the full amount from the first one with enough funds. We can’t combine multiple currencies to complete the payment. We'll check your accounts for funds in this order:
- Transaction currency
- Your base currency
- Next active currency with enough balance
If no currency has enough funds in the order above, the Direct Debit will fail. You can customise your preferred currency for a specific Direct Debit in the 'Scheduled payments' section of the Revolut app.

There are a few reasons why a Direct Debit might not have been processed when you were expecting. It could have been previously deactivated, or the merchant may have scheduled it for a different date. To check if the Direct Debit is still active, and to verify its scheduled date:

- Tap the calendar icon in the top-right corner
- Choose the transaction to view the scheduled charge date

Check the reason and refund timeframes by tapping the deposit in your in-app transactions list. The money can take up to 5 business days to be returned to your external bank account. Common reasons for failed card deposits are:
- Failed 3D secure: you didn't authenticate the deposit. Try again or with Apple/Google Pay
- Declined by your external bank
- Insufficient balance
- Restricted account: this can happen for various reasons, such as an expired document

In your Revolut app:
- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu of the Revolut app
- Go to the 'eSIM' section
- Follow the steps below

- Open settings and choose 'Networks & Internet'
- Select 'SIMs (+)' and then select a SIM
- Tap 'Next' on the 'Download your eSIM' page
- Tap 'Need help?' on the 'Scan your QR code from network page'
- Tap 'Enter it manually' on the 'Help adding a network page'
- Enter ‌the code you receive and select 'Continue', before tapping 'Download'

- Install the Revolut eSIM on your device. A banner will appear in-app guiding you through how to do this
- Select the Revolut eSIM for data roaming from your device’s settings

- Open 'Settings' and select 'Mobile Service'
- Under 'SIMs', select your newly installed eSIM (your device may automatically name your eSIM, but it won’t be your 'Primary' SIM)
- Toggle on 'Turn on this line' and then toggle on 'Data roaming' on the same page

- Tap on 'Mobile Data' and select the eSIM

- Select the amount of data you need
- Proceed to check out and purchase your plan

To remove the Revolut eSIM on iOS, go to your device settings, select ‘Mobile service’, then ‘SIMs’, choose the Revolut eSIM, and select 'Delete eSIM'.

- Open your settings
- Navigate to SIM or network settings
- Select the eSIM you want to remove
- Look for an option to remove or delete the SIM

eSIM data plans can only be used on the device they were purchased from. You can't use them on another device, even if you've downloaded the Revolut app on that device.

- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu
- Select eSIM and choose 'Get data plan'
- Select a coverage — local for one country, or regional or global for multiple countries
- Select data amount
- Continue to checkout
- Choose from your RevPoints, account balance, or both to pay for your plan and complete the purchase
The data plan’s validity period starts from the date of purchase, or when your eSIM is ready to be installed if it’s your first purchase. To request a refund, you need to contact us via our in-app chat. You can have up to 15 eSIM data plans, but only one can be used at a time.

- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu
- Tap eSIM
- Tap 'Get data plan'
- Select 'Global'
- Tap 'Global' again to see the full list of available countries

Your Revolut eSIM includes global data only. Voice calls and SMS messages are not supported, but you can use any messaging or call platform that uses data with your eSIM — for example, WhatsApp or Facebook Messenger.

"The scammers were testing thousands of numbers. Because I caught the 'penny test', I stopped them before they could make a GBP 2,000 purchase at an electronics store."

## Summary
This situation involves a highly technical and automated form of fraud known as a BIN ('issuer identification number') attack. The BIN refers to the first 6–8 digits of a credit or debit card, which are public and identify the specific issuer and card type.
Criminals use sophisticated software to generate thousands of potential combinations to guess the remaining digits of a card number, along with its expiry date and the 3-digit security code (CVV).
These attacks typically begin with what is known as a 'micro-transaction' or 'penny test'. You might notice a tiny, unrecognised charge from an unrecognised company. Once they confirm a card is live, they authorise much larger purchases before you even realise your details have been compromised.

## Common red flags
- Monitor the 'penny tests': Regularly review your transaction history for small, unrecognised charges. A tiny charge is a definitive warning sign that a criminal has successfully guessed your card details and is testing your account
- Scrutinise recurring fees: Scammers often hide unauthorised spending as small monthly 'subscriptions' (for example, GBP 4.99). Periodically check your active card subscriptions and cancel anything you did not explicitly authorise
- Verify website security: Be cautious of where you enter your card details. If a website looks unprofessional or lacks a secure https:// connection, do not enter your card information

- Use the 'Freeze' feature immediately: If you see any transaction you do not recognise, no matter how small, do not wait to contact us. Use the 'Freeze card' feature in-app instantly. This stops all further activity while you investigate

- Pay with secure digital wallets: Avoid saving your physical card details on multiple small websites. Use services like Apple Pay or Google Pay, which use tokenisation to process payments without sharing your actual card number with the merchant

answer:
Based on the provided help articles, here are the steps you can follow to manage your Direct Debits and subscriptions:

2. If you need to change the date or amount of a Direct Debit, you will need to cancel it and contact the merchant to set up a new one.

3. If you have a problem with a Direct Debit, you can open your scheduled payments or tap on a completed scheduled payment in your transactions list to get specialized support.

[Article 1] Why is my balance now negative?
## It could be a delayed payment
In areas with poor connectivity, the merchant may be unable to process the transaction or receive the payment immediately.
To complete the transaction, they might attempt to charge you again on a different day. This can result in a duplicate charge, where you see both a pending payment and a completed payment for the same merchant.
Both transactions might be reflected in your account balance, causing it to be negative. However, the pending transaction should automatically be cancelled or reversed. - Paid plan fees: if you don't have enough funds when Revolut paid plan fees are charged, it can push your account into a negative balance

## Which transaction caused a negative balance?
To check your recent transactions and see which one may have brought your account into a negative balance, follow these steps in-app:
- Go to 'Home' on the bottom menu
- Open your transactions listhttps://app.revolut.com/transactionsrevolut://app/transaction-list
- Review all your recent transactions in each currency account
- Based on the negative balance and recent transactions, try to calculate or identify which transaction was the one to make your balance turn negative

## What happens if my balance goes negative?
We'll try to use money from your other currency accounts to bring your account back to a positive balance. If there isn’t enough money in your other currency accounts, we'll ask you to add money to your account the next day. ## If you see a delayed transaction in-app
- Check previous transactions: review your transaction historyhttps://app.revolut.com/transactionsrevolut://app/transaction-list to see if you previously made a payment to the same merchant. ## Reasons for a negative balance in your joint account
- An authorisation payment amount was less than the final amount of the transaction
- You incur fees for Revolut services 
- A card payment has been delayed
Once your balance becomes negative, we'll notify you in-app. You’ll have 7 business days to add money.

## What happens next?
We’ll try to correct the balance automatically by:
- Taking funds from your personal account
- Withdrawing funds from your Pockets 
- Taking the equivalent value from money you hold in another currency account
- Taking the amount you owe from your stored card
We may take these steps for any of the account holders. We'll let you know when the recovery is successful. We'll never use the money in your joint account to offset an amount owed to us on your personal account. When you add money to your Revolut account using an external card, sometimes the bank may revert the transaction. This is known as a top-up chargeback. If your bank issues a top-up chargeback, the funds will be temporarily blocked on your Revolut account while the transaction is disputed.
- If the bank you transferred money from wins the dispute, the deposit amount will be refunded to the account you topped up from
- If they lose the dispute, the deposit in your Revolut account will be unblocked
For more detailed information and updates on your dispute, contact your bank.

- O cartão que você está tentando adicionar não pode estar congelado ou terminado.

Se o número do seu cartão Apple Pay for diferente do Revolut, isso é por motivos de segurança. Os últimos quatro dígitos mostrados para transações Apple Pay em seu extrato não são os últimos quatro dígitos reais do seu cartão. Em vez disso, eles representam um número criptografado. Isso garante que, mesmo se um terminal de pagamento ou banco de dados for violado, os hackers só receberão um código de segurança dinâmico de uso único, que é inútil para eles. - Abra sua carteira digital em seu iPhone
- Selecione seu cartão Revolut
- Toque nos três pontos no canto superior direito
- Escolha 'Número do cartão' para ver o número mascarado que a Apple usa para transações.

Para configurar o Apple Pay no aplicativo Revolut:
- Vá para 'Início' no menu inferior
- Toque no ícone de cartões no canto superior direito
- Selecione o cartão que deseja adicionar
- Toque em 'Adicionar ao Apple Wallet'.

- Abra sua carteira
- Toque em '+' no canto superior direito
- Selecione 'Cartão de débito ou crédito'
- Digitalize ou insira os detalhes manualmente.

Verificação no aplicativo:
- Do aplicativo da sua carteira, você será redirecionado para o aplicativo Revolut
- Faça login no aplicativo Revolut
- Toque em 'Confirmar'.

- Toque na notificação enviada para o seu telefone onde o aplicativo Revolut está instalado
- Você será redirecionado automaticamente para fazer login no aplicativo Revolut
- Quando você abrir o aplicativo, uma janela pop-up aparecerá com uma senha de uso único (OTP). Copie este OTP e cole-o no aplicativo da sua carteira para concluir a verificação.

- iPhone SE ou modelos mais recentes
- iPad 3 ou modelos mais recentes
- Todos os modelos do Apple Watch
- Modelos Mac com Touch ID.

- Ter passado pela verificação de identidade
- Não ter saldo negativo na conta
- Usar um cartão não descartável (físico ou virtual)
- Ter a idade mínima necessária para usar o Apple Pay em seu país.

A performance dos cartões sem contato pode variar com base no design do cartão, por exemplo, dependendo do material do cartão ou da localização da antena. Como resultado, alguns cartões se conectam mais facilmente do que outros.

Se você tiver problemas para aceitar um pagamento sem contato:
- Peça ao cliente para segurar o cartão de pagamento sem contato diretamente em cima do seu iPhone, alinhando o chip com a borda da área de toque por vários segundos
- Se o cartão ainda não for lido, peça ao cliente para deslizar o chip diretamente sobre o entalhe do seu dispositivo
- Certifique-se de que o aplicativo Revolut Business e o telefone estão na última versão do iOS
- Confirme se você aceitou os termos do Tap to Pay no iPhone via Apple Business Connect.

Se o seu iPhone disser 'Tente um cartão diferente':
Isso significa que o cartão do cliente não é suportado. A Revolut suporta pagamentos com cartões de débito e crédito Mastercard, Visa e American Express, além de Apple Pay, Google Pay e outras carteiras digitais. Para usar o Tap to Pay no iPhone, você deve ter a permissão 'Criar pagamentos em lojas' atribuída ao seu perfil. Peça ao proprietário do seu negócio ou administrador da conta para atribuir as permissões corretas ao seu perfil.

- Você não está em um país suportado para usar nosso produto. Revise nossos termos e condições em https://www.revolut.com/legal/tap-to-pay/ para obter mais informações.
- Você está usando uma conexão de roaming ou uma VPN, que pode restringir o acesso a este serviço.
- O banco do seu cliente recusou a transação. Peça a eles para tentar novamente com um cartão diferente.

[Article 4] Strange small charges on your card?
"I noticed a transaction for GBP 0.15 from a company abroad. I almost ignored it because it was so small. But then I saw another one for GBP 1.00. I froze my card through the Revolut app and called the fraud team. It turned out my card was part of a 'BIN attack'."
"The scammers were testing thousands of numbers. Because I caught the 'penny test', I stopped them before they could make a GBP 2,000 purchase at an electronics store."

## Summary
This situation involves a highly technical and automated form of fraud known as a BIN ('issuer identification number') attack. The BIN refers to the first 6–8 digits of a credit or debit card, which are public and identify the specific issuer and card type.
Criminals use sophisticated software to generate thousands of potential combinations to guess the remaining digits of a card number, along with its expiry date and the 3-digit security code (CVV).
These attacks typically begin with what is known as a 'micro-transaction' or 'penny test'. You might notice a tiny, unrecognised charge from an unrecognised company. Once they confirm a card is live, they authorise much larger purchases before you even realise your details have been compromised.

## Common red flags
- Monitor the 'penny tests': Regularly review your transaction history for small, unrecognised charges. A tiny charge is a definitive warning sign that a criminal has successfully guessed your card details and is testing your account
- Scrutinise recurring fees: Scammers often hide unauthorised spending as small monthly 'subscriptions' (for example, GBP 4.99). Periodically check your active card subscriptions and cancel anything you did not explicitly authorise
- Verify website security: Be cautious of where you enter your card details. If a website looks unprofessional or lacks a secure https:// connection, do not enter your card information

## Safety best practices
- Use the 'Freeze' feature immediately: If you see any transaction you do not recognise, no matter how small, do not wait to contact us. Use the 'Freeze card' feature in-app instantly. This stops all further activity while you investigate
- Use virtual cards for online shopping: For purchases on new or less-familiar websites, use a virtual or disposable card. These have a different number from your physical card. If a virtual card is caught in an attack, you can simply delete it and create a new one without affecting your main card
- Pay with secure digital wallets: Avoid saving your physical card details on multiple small websites. Use services like Apple Pay or Google Pay, which use tokenisation to process payments without sharing your actual card number with the merchant

To check if you have an active eSIM plan, go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu. Tap 'eSIM' to view any active plans. Make sure to turn on data roaming for the eSIM you're using by going to the network/SIM settings in your phone.

## Make sure your eSIM is installed
You must have purchased a data plan first to be able to install your Revolut eSIM. Once you've purchased your data plan and your eSIM is ready to use, you'll be prompted to install it. eSIMs can only be installed and activated on the device they were purchased on.

## How to set up APN for Android users
- Open your device's settings and select 'Connections'
- Tap 'Mobile networks' and choose 'Access Point Names'
- Select 'eSIM'
- Check if the 'truphone.com' APN is set. If it isn't, go to 'Access Point Names' and select 'eSIM'
- Tap 'Add' and enter 'Revolut' in the 'Name' field
- In the 'APN' field, enter 'truphone.com' and save it
- Select the 'Revolut' APN for your eSIM

## Check your coverage
If you've completed the above steps and still can't access your data, you may be in an area with limited mobile coverage, or no coverage. Try changing locations and make sure you have enough signal to connect to your data network.
Switch your phone to 'Airplane mode' or turn it off and on again to restart the signal search.

[Article 2] Installing and activating my eSIM
To install your Revolut eSIM, you’ll need to purchase a data plan first. This plan will decide how much data your eSIM comes loaded with. You can always add more data to your plan later, if you need it. eSIM is provided by Revolut Ltd.

## How to install your eSIM
In your Revolut app:
- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu of the Revolut app
- Go to the 'eSIM' section
- Follow the steps below
Installing an eSIM on iOS: Tap 'Install' on the 'eSIM' section in your Revolut app.
Installing an eSIM on Android:
- Open settings and choose 'Networks & Internet'
- Select 'SIMs (+)' and then select a SIM
- Tap 'Next' on the 'Download your eSIM' page
- Tap 'Need help?' on the 'Scan your QR code from network page'
- Tap 'Enter it manually' on the 'Help adding a network page'
- Enter ‌the code you receive and select 'Continue', before tapping 'Download'
Depending on your phone manufacturer, the instructions for Android may differ.

## How to activate your data plan
- Install the Revolut eSIM on your device. A banner will appear in-app guiding you through how to do this
- Select the Revolut eSIM for data roaming from your device’s settings

## How to select a Revolut eSIM for data roaming
On iOS devices:
- Open 'Settings' and select 'Mobile Service'
- Under 'SIMs', select your newly installed eSIM (your device may automatically name your eSIM, but it won’t be your 'Primary' SIM)
- Toggle on 'Turn on this line' and then toggle on 'Data roaming' on the same page 
- Go back to the previous 'Mobile Service' page
- Tap on 'Mobile Data' and select the eSIM 
On Android devices:
- Open 'Settings' and choose 'Networks & Internet'
- Select 'SIMs' and tap 'Revolut' which is your downloaded eSIM
- Toggle 'Use SIM' on, then toggle 'Mobile data' on, then toggle 'Roaming' on
Depending on your phone manufacturer, the instructions for Android may differ.

[Article 3] Revolut data plans
eSIM allows you to activate a mobile data plan in a specific country from a network provider without having to use a physical SIM card. You can buy a data plan anytime before or during your trip. Your plan activates as soon as you complete your purchase and install your eSIM.
Your eSIM data plan is provided by one of our partners, 1Global or Gigs. Revolut Ltd is an agent of 1Global and Gigs. When you purchase an eSIM data plan through the Revolut app, the fee for the eSIM data plan is payable to the partner.
The Revolut entity that you hold an account with will provide you with the underlying payment services. ## Purchase data plans
- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu
- Select eSIM and choose 'Get data plan'
- Select a coverage — local for one country, or regional or global for multiple countries
- Select data amount
- Continue to checkout
- Choose from your RevPoints, account balance, or both to pay for your plan and complete the purchase
The data plan’s validity period starts from the date of purchase, or when your eSIM is ready to be installed if it’s your first purchase. To request a refund, you need to contact us via our in-app chat. You can have up to 15 eSIM data plans, but only one can be used at a time.
Plans appear on the eSIM page in-app, with the most local one taking priority. New plans for the same area activate after the current plan expires. When a plan runs out of data, it moves to 'Expired plans', and the app switches to the next one automatically.

## Available countries
To see available countries regionally and globally in-app:
- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu
- Tap eSIM
- Tap 'Get data plan'
- Select 'Global'
- Tap 'Global' again to see the full list of available countries

## Can I access network voice calls and SMS on eSIMs?
Your Revolut eSIM includes global data only. Voice calls and SMS messages are not supported, but you can use any messaging or call platform that uses data with your eSIM — for example, WhatsApp or Facebook Messenger.

---

[Article 4] Managing my eSIM data plan
## Top up your data plan
In the Revolut app:
- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu
- Tap 'eSIM' and 'Get data plan'
- Choose your desired coverage — local for one country, or regional/global for multiple countries
- Select the amount of data you need
- Proceed to check out and purchase your plan
To receive an invoice for your eSIM purchase, request live support by typing 'Live agent' in the in-app chat.

## How to check how much data you've used
In the Revolut app:
- Go to 'RevPoints' on the bottom menu
- Tap 'eSIM' and select one of your active plans
- You'll see the remaining data and total data used
If you have notifications enabled on your device, you'll receive a notification when you've used 80% of your data. You'll receive another notification when your data has run out.

## Deleting an eSIM
To remove the Revolut eSIM on iOS, go to your device settings, select ‘Mobile service’, then ‘SIMs’, choose the Revolut eSIM, and select 'Delete eSIM'.
The steps to remove an eSIM on Android may vary slightly depending on the manufacturer and model, but the general process is:
- Open your settings
- Navigate to SIM or network settings
- Select the eSIM you want to remove
- Look for an option to remove or delete the SIM

## Can I transfer an eSIM data plan to another phone?
eSIM data plans can only be used on the device they were purchased from. You can't use them on another device, even if you've downloaded the Revolut app on that device.
If you need another eSIM for a second device, you'll need to purchase one directly from the Revolut app on that device.

- The address may not have been entered correctly
- The address may not be compatible with the selected cryptocurrency or network
- Revolut may be performing additional security checks on the withdrawal
- The withdrawal may be below the minimum threshold
- The withdrawal may not have been confirmed on the blockchain yet
- There may be technical issues with the withdrawal

Revolut is designed to complete genuine transfers promptly. Read more in this blog posthttps://www.revolut.com/blog/post/crypto-trust-uk/.

## Input information correctly
When attempting to withdraw crypto, it's important to carefully double-check all the information you enter to avoid potential losses. This includes:
- Making sure the address is entered correctly
- Make sure you're transferring on the chain of the recipient wallet

## Respond to us truthfully
If we request additional information from you, it’s because we're trying to protect you. If you don't respond, the withdrawal will be cancelled. There's no impact on your account if this happens. However, if you respond untruthfully, there's a risk you might lose your funds. 

## Don't transact with unknown addresses
If we see a transfer towards an address we think is suspicious, we have the right to cancel it. In very rare circumstances, such as illegal activity, we may restrict or close your account. This is only done as a last resort.

---

[Article 2] How to ensure my crypto is transferred successfully?
Revolut is designed to complete genuine transfers immediately, with 95% of transactions completed within 1 minute. Only 4.1% of transactions require additional checks, which are typically completed within 3 hours. For less than 1% of transactions, we may require more information to process. 

## How to complete crypto deposits
It's important to carefully check all the information you enter to avoid potential losses. Make sure:
- Your Revolut deposit address has been pasted correctly in the external sending wallet
- You transfer a token Revolut supports
- You transfer on a chain Revolut supports

## How to complete crypto withdrawals
It's important to carefully check all the information you enter to avoid potential losses. Make sure:
- Receiving address has been pasted correctly in send flow
- The address is compatible with the selected cryptocurrency or is on a correct network
If we detect a scam or potential fraud during a withdrawal, we trigger additional questions to raise your awareness and protect you from potential loss. Always answer carefully and remain vigilant.

## If further information is requested
We'll send you a notification, as well as display in-app banners, to get your attention if we need additional information. Just tap the notifications to see exactly what's required from you.
The additional information should be straightforward. For example, a bank statement that shows proof of funds, so we can ensure the source of the payment is genuine. We explain crypto transfers and withdrawals in more detail in this blog posthttps://www.revolut.com/blog/post/crypto-trust-uk/?geo-redirect=true.

---

[Article 3] Pending crypto deposits
You can see the reason why your deposit is pending on the transaction details screen. To see the status of your deposit:
- Go to 'Crypto' on the bottom menu
- Scroll to your transactions list or select the crypto you deposited
- Find your deposit transaction
- Tap on it to see the details of pending reason
Your crypto deposit could be pending for a number of reasons.

## Internal checks
Revolut performs automatic internal checks on every deposit, which are typically completed within minutes. However, in rare cases where additional information is needed, the process can take longer.
If we need more information about your deposit, a banner will appear on your home screen. You can tap and follow the steps on screen to provide what's requested. Once you submit the information, it may take up to 3 working days for us to verify it.

## Deposit is below minimum threshold
If your deposit is below the required minimum, it won't be added to your balance right away. To fix this:
- Make another deposit in the same cryptocurrency and on the same network to meet the minimum amount
- Deposits on different networks won't count toward the same minimum. For example, if you made a deposit on the Tron network, adding funds on the Ethereum network won't help meet the minimum requirement
- The total balance will be credited in one consolidated deposit once the minimum is reached
- There is no time limit to meet the minimum deposit requirement
- For the latest information on minimum deposits for specific tokens, visit the respective crypto section for the token or refer to our T&Cshttps://www.revolut.com/legal/cryptocurrency-terms/?geo-redirect=true.

## Deposit not yet confirmed on the blockchain
If your deposit isn't confirmed on the blockchain, you can track its status using the transaction hash on a blockchain explorer. If a transaction remains in 'Confirming' or 'Pending' status for too long, it may be due to low network fees.
Blockchain settlement can take anywhere from a few minutes to 2 hours, depending on the network's activity. The amount of confirmations we require to consider a transfer final varies per blockchain. To see details on the blockchain explorer:
- Go to 'Crypto' on the bottom menu
- Scroll down to select your transaction or select the crypto you are depositing and find your pending transaction there
- Tap 'Blockchain hash'
- Choose 'View my transaction' to see details on the blockchain explorer

## We are experiencing technical issues
In very rare cases, deposits might take longer than expected due to technical issues. If this happens, we will notify you in-app.

---

[Article 4] Can't see my deposit in-app
Your deposit may not be appearing in your Revolut app due to one of the reasons detailed below.

## Deposits on a network or crypto that Revolut doesn't support
Deposits of unsupported tokens or via unsupported networks won't be processed, and funds won't be added to your balance.
Even though such transactions might appear as completed on the blockchain, Revolut doesn't receive these transactions because it doesn't interact with blockchains or token contracts it doesn't support. [Article 2] Problem with a Direct Debit
## Insufficient funds for a Direct Debit
If you don’t have enough funds in the Direct Debit currency, we’ll check other currency balances in the order below, and take the full amount from the first one with enough funds. We can’t combine multiple currencies to complete the payment. We'll check your accounts for funds in this order:
- Transaction currency
- Your base currency
- Next active currency with enough balance
If no currency has enough funds in the order above, the Direct Debit will fail. You can customise your preferred currency for a specific Direct Debit in the 'Scheduled payments' section of the Revolut app.

## Direct Debit didn't trigger
There are a few reasons why a Direct Debit might not have been processed when you were expecting. It could have been previously deactivated, or the merchant may have scheduled it for a different date. To check if the Direct Debit is still active, and to verify its scheduled date:
- Go to 'Payments' on the bottom menu
- Tap the calendar icon in the top-right corner
- Choose the transaction to view the scheduled charge date
If you can't see the transfer, it was either disabled, or it wasn't successfully created in the first place. In these cases, contact the merchant directly to clarify the situation, or set it up again.

## Direct Debit failed or reverted
Check to see why your Direct Debit failed or was reverted in your transactions list. Just tap on the unsuccessful transaction for more info.

## Dispute a Direct Debit
Tap ‌the Direct Debit in your transactions list and choose the problem you're experiencing. You can then follow the prompts to dispute the Direct Debit.

---

## How to view my Direct Debits
- Go to 'Payments' on the bottom menu
- Tap on the calendar icon in the top-right
- View active Direct Debits

## Cancel a Direct Debit
- Go to 'Payments' on the bottom menu
- Tap on the calendar icon in the top-right
- Tap on an active Direct Debit
- Tap 'Cancel future payments'

## Change the date or amount of a Direct Debit
Revolut can't change the amount or ‌date of a Direct Debit. You must cancel it and contact the merchant to set up a new Direct Debit.

## Problems with a Direct Debit
If you have a problem with your Direct Debit, open your scheduled payments or tap on a completed scheduled payment in your transactions list to get specialised support.
If you need more help with a Direct Debit, read this FAQ.

[Article 4] How to split a bill with another Revolut customer
- In your transactions list, tap the payment you want to split
- Tap 'Split bill'
- Select the Revolut friend or contact you want to split it with and tap 'Continue'
